# JEVision

> JEVision is a free, open-source (MIT) macOS app for visual UI testing of any Mac application, including apps you don't own and can't instrument. It sees the screen and uses the real mouse and keyboard, the way a person does. A test is a flowchart: one JSON file (`*.flow.json`) per test, with a block for every step.

It is written in Rust (the core: file format, validation, runner, reports, MCP server) and SwiftUI (the Mac app), runs on macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon and Intel, and is available in English and Russian. Tests, screenshots and reports stay on the Mac; a screenshot leaves it only for a cloud AI model (a check by meaning, or finding an element described in words), after masking, or in a bug report filed on GitHub.

## What it does
- Flowchart editor: add, connect and edit blocks on a canvas; every change is saved and can be undone; problems are shown on the block they concern. Space opens the block library, right-clicking the canvas places a block there, and ⌘K opens a command palette that finds any command, block or test.
- Notes on the canvas: Markdown notes about the test, a folder or a block (a block's note moves with it), with attached files and links (GitHub issues show their title and state), replies, @mentions, a resolved mark and a history taken from git; files live in `<test>.assets/notes/<id>/`, big ones can go to Git LFS.
- Stable screenshots: an `openApp` block can quit a running copy and start fresh (`"resetState": true`) and fix the window of the app (`"windowSize": {"width": 900, "height": 640}`, `"windowPosition": {"x": 80, "y": 60}`, in points); checks look only at the window of the app under test, and in dark appearance a check saves `name.dark.png` as a new reference instead of comparing with the light one. One run at a time uses the mouse and keyboard: the app, `jevision run` and `jevision mcp` share a lock (`~/Library/Application Support/JEVision/screen.lock`), a test that uses the screen waits and says who has it ("Screen busy: JEVision, test Sign in, since 12:03"), tests that don't use the screen never wait.
- Branching: an `if` block can have several conditions (`then`, `elseIf1`, `elseIf2`… and `else`); the first condition the screen matches wins.
- Recording: clicks, typing and key presses in the app under test become blocks with a picture of the target; passwords become secrets kept in the Keychain.
- Custom blocks: a test other tests run with `runTest`, with values in `inputs` that the block reads as `${input.NAME}`; make one from selected blocks (Make Block…, saved as `blocks/NAME.block.json`) and share it (File → Custom Blocks… → Share…) as a package, a folder `ID.jevblock/` with `block.json` (id like `com.acme.sign-in`, name, description, icon, semantic version, author, license, `minVersion`, `inputs` with `label` and `default`, `dependencies`) and `flow.json` (the steps) next to its pictures. Packages install from a folder, a .zip file or an https address (GitHub repository, a folder in one as `/tree/REF/PATH`, or a release) with File → Install Block… or `jevision blocks install`; one source can hold several packages (a `blocks/` folder of `.jevblock` folders, or several `.jevblock.zip` release files), shown as a list with a check box and "what it does" for each. Before anything is installed the person reads what the block does, with scripts, network requests, databases, opened apps and typing marked. Packages aren't signed: id and author are claimed, not proven. A package runs another with a `runTest` of `../ID.jevblock/flow.json` and lists it in `dependencies: [{id, version?: range like ^1.2.0 / ~1.2.0 / 1.x / >=1.2.0 <2.0.0, source?: https address}]`; installing needs each dependency installed or in the same source in a version that fits, dependencies install first, a circle is an error, and a test running a package with unmet dependencies is an error. Installed blocks are in `blocks/ID.jevblock/` of the project and listed under Community; they are read-only, and "Make This a Block of the Project…" copies one into `blocks/NAME.block.json` and can switch the tests to the copy. `jevision.blocks.json` keeps where they came from (`sources`) and which version (`versions`); opening a project offers to install the missing ones again (`jevision blocks restore`), and a version that changed at its address needs `--force`. Reports name the package and its version. A `runTest` of a package keeps `package: {version, source?}`; if the package isn't installed, validation says "This step needs the block “ID VERSION”, which isn't installed in this project" and offers Install… (CLI: prints `jevision blocks install SOURCE`).
- Boards: the All Tests board shows every test with its last result, flaky and quarantined ones marked; people add boards of their own with notes, frames, pictures and links. Each board is a `boards/NAME.canvas` file in the open JSON Canvas 1.0 format, so Obsidian opens it too.
- Running: run a test, step through it (⌥⌘R) or start from any block, with breakpoints; moving the mouse pauses, Esc twice stops. Optional video of every run.
- Reports and history: a screenshot of every step; checks show the screen, the reference image and their differences; "Accept New Reference" in a failed check's report replaces the picture and, when several tests share it, lists every block that uses it (also the `.dark` version) and asks to confirm, edit or skip each one's areas, masks and threshold first (nothing is written until the end; Undo restores it all; there is no CLI command for it); export as HTML or JUnit XML; flaky tests are detected from history, per data row.
- Find by description: a click or typing can target an element described in words (`{ "description": "the blue Save button" }`); JEV by TypeSafe AI finds it on the masked screenshot, called with a TypeSafe AI key or through Cloudflare Workers AI (`jev-cloudflare`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and the account ID in `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`).
- Checks by meaning: describe the screen in words and an AI model decides (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, JEV by TypeSafe AI directly or through Cloudflare Workers AI, Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible server); a check can require JEV to be at least as sure as its `confidence`.
- Environments (`jevision.environments.json`), data-driven tests from CSV (`useData`), retries and quarantine (`jevision.project.json`; quarantine can end on a date, and the app suggests it for a test that was unreliable 3 times in 7 days), schedules (`jevision.schedule.json`), run notifications to Slack, Telegram or email (`jevision.notifications.json`, one summary per batch, secrets in the Keychain or in `JEVISION_SLACK_WEBHOOK`, `JEVISION_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`, `JEVISION_SMTP_PASSWORD`; `--no-notify` turns them off).
- Git and GitHub inside the app: commit, pull, push, branches, a visual diff of tests and pictures, pull requests. Report Bug… on a failed run (or `jevision issue`) files a GitHub issue with the steps, the cause and screenshots of the failed step, or adds the run to an open issue about the same failure; secrets are masked and screenshots go to the repository's `jevision-attachments` branch. Sign in under Settings → Git and GitHub through GitHub CLI or, with your own OAuth app's Client ID, in the browser; the token is kept in the Keychain, and on CI comes from `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- CI: the generated GitHub Actions workflow uploads the artifact `jevision-reports` (JUnit, HTML and the run reports). `jevision run` in CI records the CI system, repository, branch, commit, pull request and run page in each report. Signed in to GitHub, the app fetches those runs into the Runs list (marked "CI · pull request #N" or "CI · branch X", each once), and a filter shows runs by This Mac, Schedule, iPhone or CI.
- iPhone remote: browse tests and their cards, read the canvas's sticky notes (Markdown text, replies, links and attachment names, read-only; files stay on the Mac; a switch hides resolved notes), start a run (or one row of its data table), follow it (including when it waits for the Mac's screen) and read reports from a paired iPhone.

## Block types
`openApp`, `openFile`, `click`, `hover`, `drag`, `scroll`, `type`, `pressKeys`, `waitFor`, `pause`, `check`, `if`, `repeat`, `useData`, `runTest`, `script`, `command`, `http`, `checkFile`, `database`, `clipboard`, `dateTime`. `click`, `hover`, `drag` and `scroll` can hold ⌃ ⌥ ⇧ ⌘ (`"modifiers": ["cmd"]`; ⌘ with `scroll` zooms in most apps) and `click` and `drag` can use the `"right"` or `"middle"` button; a target is `{ "image" }`, `{ "description" }`, `{ "element": { "id", "role", "title", "index" } }` (an interface element found by macOS accessibility: at least one of id, role such as `button` or `textField`, and title, the exact label; `index` from 0 picks one of several matches), `{ "point": {x, y} }` or `{ "area": "x,y,width,height" }` (fractions of the window, the middle is used); `check`, `if` and `waitFor` (`"until": { "element": … }`) take an element check, the element with `"is"`: `present`, `absent`, `enabled`, `disabled`, `selected`, `notSelected`, `valueEquals`, `valueContains`, `titleEquals` or `titleContains` with `"to"`, and a failure says what was found instead; `openApp` can pass `"arguments": ["--demo"]` and `"environment": { "API_URL": "${env.API_URL}" }` to a copy it starts, and a target picture, a target area or a `check` reference picture can be a variable (`{ "image": "${var.shot}" }`, `{ "area": "${var.box}" }`, type-checked while editing; such a picture has no `.dark` version and is never saved from the screen); a `script` takes typed inputs and gives typed outputs (text, number, boolean, image, area); `clipboard` puts text or a PNG picture (`image`), reads its text, picture (`"content": "image"`, a PNG saved with the run) or copied files (`"content": "files"`, one path a line) into a variable, or checks its text; `dateTime` keeps the date and time, moved by an amount, as a variable, with month and day names in `"language": "en"` or `"ru"` (`%B`, `%b`, `%A`, `%a`; Russian `%OB` is the month by itself; `%^B` in capitals) and in any `"timeZone"` such as `"Europe/Berlin"`. Secrets are referenced as `${secret.NAME}`, environment values as `${env.NAME}` (`${env.ENVIRONMENT}` is the environment's own name, so an `if` block can branch on it: `"value": { "of": "${env.ENVIRONMENT}", "is": "equals", "to": "prod" }`), data columns as `${data.COLUMN}`. A recorded test is laid out in rows of three blocks; the editor's Arrange in Rows does it for any test.

## Command line
- `jevision run <tests> [--env NAME] [--rows 2-4] [--retries N] [--type T] [--priority P] [--status S] [--author NAME] [--flaky] [--parallel [N]] [--junit FILE] [--html DIR] [--video MODE] [--json]`: run tests and save reports; `--parallel` runs tests that leave the screen alone side by side (tests that use it take turns). The filters keep only tests whose card says so. Exit status 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 can't run.
- Every command takes `--lang CODE`: the language of its messages and of the reports it writes (`en`, `ru`, any language of the app's string catalog). Without it: the Mac's language, English when the `CI` variable is set. JSON output (except a failure's `message`), issue codes and option names never change with the language.
- `jevision validate <tests>`: report errors and warnings.
- `jevision fmt <tests> [--check]`: rewrite files in canonical form.
- `jevision blocks list | install <folder, .zip or https address> [--only ID,…] [--yes] [--force] | update [ID] [--yes] [--force] | remove ID [--force] | restore [--only ID,…] [--yes] [--force] [--project DIR]`: manage blocks others shared; `install` prints what each block of the source does and installs only with `--yes`; `restore` installs again what `jevision.blocks.json` lists and the project lacks, printing the plan without `--yes` ("Everything in jevision.blocks.json is installed already." when there is nothing to do).
- `jevision issue [<test or run>] [--send] [--title TEXT] [--comment-on N | --new] [--project DIR]`: print a bug report about the newest failed run; `--send` files it as a GitHub issue. Exit status 1 when an issue about the same failure is open and neither `--comment-on` nor `--new` is given.
- `jevision schedule run <project>`: run the project's schedules that are due.
- `jevision mcp [--project DIR]`: Model Context Protocol server over standard input and output. `jevision mcp --pair LINK` pairs this computer with another Mac and `jevision mcp --remote MAC` serves an assistant with that Mac's tests (`--forget MAC` removes it).

## MCP tools
`list_tests`, `read_test`, `write_test`, `add_blocks`, `remove_block`, `validate_test`, `list_block_types`, `run_test`, `get_run`, `stop_run`, `get_report`, `screenshot`, `draft_bug_report`, `send_bug_report`. `send_bug_report` files a GitHub issue with the failed step's masked screenshots. Running tests and screenshots are off until the user turns them on in Settings → AI → Assistants. Each run an assistant starts is confirmed by the user in an alert in the app, unless they turned that off; no answer within a minute is a refusal. The app lists the assistants that connected.

## Build
`git clone https://github.com/dev-pikapik/JEVision.git && cd JEVision && apps/macos/scripts/build.sh` (Xcode 26+, Rust 1.85+); the app appears at `apps/macos/build/JEVision.app`.
